newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian palm oil prices soften in late trading.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian palm oil prices soften in late trading.

text.p: Indonesian crude palm oil and olein prices softened further in late Monday trading following a decline in the Malaysian market, traders said.
They said a bearish crop report from the Malaysian palm oil authority seemed to have spilled-over to Indonesian domestic markets and pulled prices down slightly.
One trader in Medan said the crop report and expectation of a possible intervention from state commodity regulator Bulog were still haunting the market.
"Buyers have shunned the market in the short-term and will only buy now at a lower price level. We are going to see some correction before prices stabilise again," he said.
Traders said some buying interest of crude palm oil was seen at around 1,210 rupiah/kg, compared with some selling interest at around 1,220 rupiah/kg.
Olein was quoted at 1,410 rupiah/kg in Medan, compared with 1,425 rupiah/kg in the morning. It was quoted at around 1,440-50 rupiah/kg in Jakarta and Surabaya.
